title: Investigation of the effects of ultra-dry process atmospheres including human factors in battery production
summary: As global demand for energy storage solutions continues to rise, the production of lithium-ion batteries is becoming increasingly important. Along with this, the number of jobs in dry rooms where relative humidity is close to 0% is also on the rise. Despite this growing relevance, there is still little research on the effects of these ultra-dry conditions on humans. The project systematically investigates the health and performance-related effects of this ultra-dry work environment on employees, thereby providing the basis for practical occupational health and safety measures.
conditions: Health complaints and performance issues among battery production workers caused by extremely dry work environments.

interventions.name:
Substudy 1 (non-interventional, cross-sectional): Survey of employees working in ultra-dry process atmospheres on exposure characteristics and health complaints
Substudy 2 (interventional, longitudinal, without control ): Ambulatory assessment of battery cell production workers over 10 working days

Substudy 3: Normal-dry indoor air condition
Substudy 5: First PSA variant recompiled or developed based on the study results

Substudy 3: ultra-dry indoor air condition
Substudy 5: Second PSA variant recompiled or developed based on the study results

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Substudies 1 and 4: Employees who work in ultra-dry rooms at least occasionally (once a month)
Substudy 2: Employees who work in dry rooms for at least 4 hours a day during the two-week assessment period
Substudy 3: a) Employees from all occupational groups with no previous experience of working in ultra-dry rooms, b) employees in the age group of average workers (~ 44 years)
Substudy 5: People with no previous experience of working in ultra-dry rooms.
Exclusion criteria:
Substudies 1 and 4:  Employees who never work in ultra-dry rooms
Substudy 2:  a) Employees who work in ultra-dry rooms less frequently than defined in the inclusion criteria; b) Employees with acute colds/flu symptoms
Substudy 3:  a) Employees with previous experience of working in ultra-dry rooms; b)  People not in employment; c) People aged under 30 and over 55; d) People with pre-existing conditions affecting the skin (atopic dermatitis), eyes (conjunctivitis) or respiratory tract (asthma); e) People with acute colds/flu symptoms; f) People with claustrophobia
Substudy 5: People with previous experience and/or currently working in ultra-dry rooms
Substudies 4 and 5:  a) People with pre-existing skin, eye or respiratory conditions; b) People with acute colds/flu symptoms; c) People with claustrophobia
